newsitem.title: USA: CNET to unveil Online Web information service.
newsitem.headline: CNET to unveil Online Web information service.

text.p: CNET Inc. said it will announce the launch Monday of a wide-ranging consumer online service which will serve as a one-stop point for finding information on the World Wide Web.

The new offering, called Snap! Online, is a bid by the computer news and television production company to extend well beyond its current high tech focus, adding subjects like entertainment, sports, travel, finances and health.
Instead of aggregating information on its own site, CNET will use a team of 30 editors to update links to news and information on other sites through Snap!
The new features will rival other major media sites on the World Wide Web, including Yahoo! Inc. and Excite Inc. as well as America Online Inc. and Microsoft Corp.'s MSN.
Major Internet service providers or ISPs will participate, including AT&T Corp.'s AT&T WorldNet Service, MCI Communications Inc.'s MCI Internet and Sprint Corp.'s Sprint Internet Passport.
The ISPs could help boost usage of the new site at a time when analysts note the heaviest Internet advertising is still concentrated on a handful of the most heavily trafficked sites.
The service is designed to be customisable, enabling CNET's partners to create a co-branded consumer offering.

A CD-ROM enhancement enables CNET to take advantage of the hybrid CD-ROM and online model being heavily promoted by chipmaker Intel Corp., an investor in CNET, as a means of offering rich multimedia content.

The combination of the two sources enables a person to draw on graphics from the CD-ROM drive more rapidly than they could be accessed on-line, but still tap into up-to- date information and real-time events over the Internet.

Earthlink Network Inc. has agreed to distribute at least 10 million co-branded Earthlink/ Snap! Online CD-ROM disks containing the Snap! Online Starter Kit beginning in the fourth quarter of 1997, CNET said.

Snap! will be Earthlink's default Internet online service for existing customers, while other providers will link to a co-branded version of the product from a button prominently displayed on their home pages, CNET said.
Only Earthlink has so far agreed to distribute the CD-ROM but the Web site, (http://www.snap.com) can be accessed directly as well using different browsers.

Mindspring Enterprises, BellSouth's BellSouth.net Inc., and Concentric Network are also among those who have signed initial distribution agreements with CNET, which said it is in discussions with more than 30 ISPs, PC makers and brand marketers on further deals.

The much anticipated service raised investor worries in mid-April, however, when CNET said that out of hefty first quarter loss boosted by one time expenses, $2.2 million was spent on the previously unannounced project.

The service, which had been dubbed "Gunsmoke" in its development phase after the early American Western television series, is due to be available in September and include links to CNET's nine existing sites.
CNET Chairman and CEO Halsey Minor was due to provide further details about Snap! Online at a Monday news conference at CNET headquarters, the company said.
"Snap! Online provides a fully integrated solution for ISPs and other marketers who are focused on bringing customers onto the Internet," Minor said in a statement released ahead of the briefing.

Intel, which invested in CNET at the time of its initial public offering last summer, has been involved in the project. The world's largest chipmaker aims to boost demand for its fastest Pentium-based processors by promoting graphics-intensive multimedia applications.

Ron Whittier, Intel senior vice president and head of its content group, said CNET is developing a version of Snap! Online for PC makers designed to take full advantage of Intel's Pentium II processor introduced last month.

Earlier this month, Intel said it was investing an additional $5.3 million in CNET, raising its stake to 6 percent from 4.5 percent, saying the financing would help CNET with as-yet undisclosed projects.
